// Fixture covering all translation key detection patterns.
// Each line demonstrates one way a key can appear in source code.

// 1. Single quotes: t('key')
const a = t('common.buttons.create');

// 2. Double quotes: t("key")
const b = t("common.buttons.cancel");

// 3. Backtick static: t(`key`)
const c = t(`common.buttons.delete`);

// 4. Multiline call — key on next line after t(
const d = t(
  'common.buttons.edit',
);

// 5. Key in a data structure, passed to t() indirectly (e.g. category label)
const category = { label: 'apps.title' };

// 6. i18nKey prop
const e = <Trans i18nKey="upload-yaml.info" />;

// 7. Template literal with interpolation: t(`prefix.${expr}`)
const suffix = 'ago';
const f1 = t(`common.value-units.seconds-${suffix}`);
const f2 = t(`common.value-units.minutes-${suffix}`);

// 8. String concatenation: t('prefix.' + expr)
const name = 'minute';
const g = t('cron-jobs.create-modal.' + name);

// 9. tExt variant with template literal
const h = tExt(`extensibility.sections.${key}`);

// This key should NOT be detected — it is never referenced:
// unused.key.example
